title: Different terms and strategies in the battle of forms
shortTitle: Different terms and strategies in the battle of forms
summary: The notes separate the statutory ambiguity, judicial role, and commercial incentives.
notes: Northrop applies an Illinois prediction rather than its preferred approach. The following materials debate the effects of defaults on buyers and sellers, discuss the drafting history’s uncertainty, and contrast making the other side accept one’s terms with avoiding the other side’s terms. Master agreements, association rules, and electronic interchange can reduce reliance on competing forms. The Commerce & Industry problem shows a strategy’s possible adverse consequence.
